newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian PM forms leftist govt on slim majority.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian PM forms leftist govt on slim majority.

text.p: Slovenia's prime minister-designate Janez Drnovsek said on Friday he had formed a leftist government with a majority of just one after talks with three rightist parties failed earlier in the day.
"Some minutes ago my government proposal was agreed by the highest body of my party and I will hand it to the president of parliament in an hour," Drnovsek told a news conference.

Drnovsek's centre-left Liberal Democrats will form a coalition with the former communist United List of Social Democrats, the Desus party which represents pensioners, and the Nationalist Party. The government also has the support of three independent deputies, giving it 46 seats in the 90-member parliament.
"I tried all possibilities to achieve a large and strong government," Drnovsek said.

Earlier Marjan Podobnik, leader of the conservative People's Party, said the differences between the Liberal Democrats and an alliance of three rightist parties were too great and no agreement for a coalition could be found.
Drnovsek has held talks for the past two weeks to try to form a government after weeks of political deadlock which followed an inconclusive general election on November 10.
